title: English for beginners: everyday phrases
group: LANG-ENGL — English as an additional language
examples: What do I say when I meet someone in the morning?
How do I ask someone to pass me a book?

explain.say: Today we learn some useful English phrases for daily life.

items: Good morning is used in the morning.

explain.say: If it is afternoon, you should say good afternoon.
When you need help, you can say please help me.

draw.text: Asking for help: Please help me

explain.say: If you need something, you can ask 'Can you help me?'

items: This is a polite way to ask.

draw.text: Asking for help: Can you help me?

explain.say: Remember to always say please when you ask for things.
When someone gives you something, you must say thank you.

faq.q: What do I say when I meet a friend in the evening?
faq.a: You should say good evening to your friend. You can also say hello.
asks: What do I say at night?

faq.q: Is 'please' only used when I ask for things?
faq.a: No, you use it to make any request polite. It shows respect to the person.
asks: When is it okay to use please?
Does please only go with questions?

faq.q: If someone helps me, should I say thank you always?
faq.a: Yes, saying thank you is a kind thing to do. It makes the other person feel good.
asks: Do I always need to say thank you?
What is the right response to help?

faq.q: What is the difference between 'hello' and 'good morning'?
faq.a: Hello is general and can be used anytime. Good morning is specific to the morning hours.
asks: Can I use 'good morning' in the afternoon?

faq.q: If I ask for help, is 'excuse me' better than 'please help me'?
faq.a: Both are good, but 'please help me' is direct. 'Excuse me' is better for getting attention.
asks: Are there other ways to ask for help?

facts: Good morning is used from sunrise until noon.
Good afternoon is used from noon until sunset.

quiz.say: You are asking a teacher to open a window. What should you say?
quiz.show: A. Good morning. B. Please open the window. C. Thank you.
quiz.why: You need to make a request, and 'please' makes it polite.

wrong.0: This is a greeting, not a way to ask for help.
wrong.2: This is a greeting, not a way to ask for something.
wrong.3: This is said after someone helps you, not when you ask.

quiz.say: Your friend gives you a pencil. What should you say?
quiz.show: A. Good afternoon. B. Thank you. C. Can you help me?
quiz.why: You say thank you when someone gives you something nice.

wrong.1: This is only for greeting someone at that time.
wrong.2: This is used when you need assistance, not when receiving a gift.
wrong.3: Saying only 'please' is not enough; you need to say thank you.

quiz.say: If you need to get someone's attention to ask a question, which phrase is best?
quiz.show: A. Good evening. B. Excuse me. C. Thank you.
quiz.why: Excuse me is a polite way to get someone's attention first.

wrong.0: This is only for greeting someone at that time of day.
wrong.1: This is said after receiving help, not before asking.
wrong.2: This jumps straight to the problem without first getting attention.
